subject: zoology

mark_split.label: What the code is used for

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.49, VSAQ 59). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. BOOK WORDING: the book writes that the code 'is used to name an identified organism'; the ICZN governs ANIMAL names only (plant names are governed by the botanical code), and the card says animals.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The full form
steps.why: The four words are the mark: Code says it is a set of rules, and Zoological says the rules cover animals.
common_mistakes: Writing 'Botanical' in place of 'Zoological'. ICBN is the plant code; ICZN is the animal code.
Writing 'Classification' in place of 'Nomenclature'. The code governs naming, not grouping.
steps.memory_tip: Read the letters in order: International, Code, Zoological, Nomenclature.
steps.margin_note: One line. Write all four words in full; an abbreviation earns nothing.

steps.label: What the code is for
steps.why: A code exists so that the same animal is not called by different names in different places, so the second mark is for saying what the rules are for.
common_mistakes: Stopping at the full form. The question carries a second mark for what the code does.
steps.memory_tip: Code means rules: one animal, one accepted scientific name everywhere.
steps.margin_note: One sentence on what the code is used for. Two lines are enough.
